we propose VECoDeR which jointly learns node representation and community detection, and VECoDeR outperforms many baselines.
VECoDeRs is an effective and efficient generative model that simultaneously learns community detection and node representations.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) how to effectively learn node embeddings for graph analysis, (ii) how to leverage node embeddings for community detection, (iii) how to learn node embeddings and community assignments simultaneously.

the following questions: How to jointly learn community detection and node embedding? How to learn community-aware node embedding? How can community detection be improved using learned node embedding? How do the learned community-aware node embeddings perform in downstream tasks?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VECoDeRa is an efficient and effective model for learning community aware node representations.
VECoDeRa is a very effective, efficient and robust model that can be used to solve multiple graph analysis tasks simultaneously.
VECoDeRs joint learning framework can be used for community detection, node classification, and node embedding learning, which can be used for many downstream tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VECoDeRs are not only more effective but also more efficient in learning node embeddings and community detection.
VECoDeRa can be applied to a wide range of tasks, and is able to learn node embeddings that are useful for both community detection and node classification tasks.
VECoDeRs joint learning of node representation and community detection is a better approach than learning them separately.
The main takeaway from our work is that
community structure is a key factor for node representation learning.
community detection and node embeddings are two highly correlated tasks and VECoDeR jointly learning both tasks can significantly improve the performance of both tasks.
VECoDeRs ability to learn node representations that are community-aware can be leveraged for community detection.
